To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the highest mortality of Cx. quinquefasicatous was achieved by the binary mixture of limonone and trans-anethol (mixing ratio 1: 1) and by the binary mixture carvone and carycrol (mixing ratio of carvone and cardvacrol 1:2-3).
thymol and limonene are the most effective substances, and their combinations with trans-anethole or carvacrol are the most effective combinations.

thymol, p-cymene, trans-anthole, and limonene have the greatest acute toxicity against Cx. quinquefesciatus larvae, while the highest synergistic effect was achieved in the combinations: limonene-trans-anethole, eugenol-isoeguenol, carvona-carvacrol, and carvone-menthone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the use of EOs, and the results obtained are of practical importance for further development of new formulations for control of C. quinquefasicatus larvae.
the identification of new synergistic substances that could be used for the formulation of botanical insecticides.
the identification of substances and their combinations that can be used as a base for the development of new insecticides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synergistic and antagonizing effects of the tested aromatic compounds and their combinations can be used to develop new botanical insecticides.
the most suitable substances for use in the creation of new formulations of botanical insecticides against C. quinquefasicatus are thymol, p-cymene, limonene, and trans-anethol.
it is necessary to use more substances in combination in order to achieve higher mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the synergism between the substances in EOs could increase the effectiveness of EOs and thus reduce their concentration in formulations, which could lead to a significant reduction in production costs and thus a reduction of the price of EOs.
the synergistic effect of essential oils can be used to create more effective insecticides.
the synergism and antagonism of essential oil constituents are important factors in the development of effective formulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EOs can be used in the creation of new botanical insecticide formulations that are effective, environmentally friendly, and safe for human health.
the use of EOs as insecticides can be significantly enhanced if they are combined with other EOs.
the combination of substances in a ratio of 1:1 is the most suitable ratio for the creation of new formulations.
